analysis.note: Enclitic genitive singular; Śaṅkara glosses te as tava. The form is common to genders for the second-person pronoun; Pum is supplied contextually for Arjuna while retaining the genitive-singular construal.

Object of vyatitariṣyati; Śaṅkara explains it as an impurity/turbidity consisting in delusion and having the form of non-discrimination. The verifier reported a tool_error for this compound derivation and did not support the karmadhāraya relation; the analysis is retained on the commentary’s neuter gloss kāluṣyaṃ and the syntactic accusative object relation.

verification.detail: compound stem moha-kalila as Napumsaka/Dvitiya/Eka: pass; relation karmadharaya: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Simple future: ‘will pass beyond/cross over’; Śaṅkara glosses with vyatikramiṣyati.
Periphrastic future: ‘you will reach/attain’; Śaṅkara glosses gantāsi with prāpsyasi.
Object of gantāsi; Śaṅkara glosses as vairāgya, ‘dispassion,’ not mere despair.
Gerundive/future passive participle of √śru used substantively: ‘what is to be heard.’ The neuter is confirmed by Śaṅkara’s paraphrase śrotavyam.
Past passive participle of √śru used substantively: ‘what has been heard.’ The neuter is confirmed by Śaṅkara’s paraphrase śrutam.

justifications.decision: The enclitic te is construed as genitive singular dependent on buddhiḥ: ‘your intellect.’
The compound is taken as a karmadhāraya-like ‘delusion-impurity,’ not merely a physical ‘thicket’ or an unspecified difficulty. It is the accusative object crossed over by the intellect.
options_considered: a bahuvrīhi describing the intellect itself
justifications.chosen: moha-kalilaṃ = an impurity/turbidity consisting in delusion and non-discrimination

evidence.translation: ‘moha-kalila’ is an impurity/turbidity whose nature is delusion, whose form is non-discrimination.

evidence.quote: yena ātmānātma-viveka-bodhaṃ kaluṣīkṛtya viṣayaṃ pratyantaḥ-karaṇaṃ pravartate
evidence.translation: By it, after the cognition discriminating self and not-self has been defiled, the inner organ turns toward objects.

justifications.decision: The verb is not a mere motion verb but means that the intellect will pass beyond the delusive impurity, reaching a highly purified condition.

evidence.quote: tat tava buddhiḥ vyatitariṣyati vyatikramiṣyati, atiśuddha-bhāvam āpātryate ity arthaḥ
evidence.translation: That, your intellect, will pass beyond; that is, it will overstep it; the sense is that it comes to a state of great purity.

justifications.decision: nirveda is translated as dispassion/detachment, not as depression, despair, or simple disgust.

evidence.translation: ‘You will go/come to’ means ‘you will attain’; ‘nirveda’ means ‘dispassion.’

justifications.decision: The two genitives depend on nirveda/vairāgya and are neuter substantives. Śaṅkara further explains that both the not-yet-heard and the already-heard appear fruitless to the seeker at that point.
options_considered: masculine agreement with an implied teacher or text
justifications.chosen: śrotavyasya śrutasya ca = ‘toward what is to be heard and what has been heard’

evidence.translation: Dispassion with respect to what is to be heard and what has been heard.

evidence.quote: tadā śrotavyaṃ śrutaṃ ca te niṣphalaṃ pratibhātīty abhiprāyaḥ
evidence.translation: The purport is: then what is to be heard and what has been heard appear fruitless to you.

translation:
When your intellect (buddhi) shall pass beyond
this delusion-impurity (moha-kalila),
then you will attain dispassion (nirveda)
toward what is to be heard and what has been heard.
one_shot_delta: Without Śaṅkara, nirvedaṃ might be rendered as ‘despair’ or ‘disgust’; the commentary fixes it as vairāgya, dispassion.

A commentary-blind translation might leave moha-kalilaṃ as a vague ‘mire/thicket of delusion’; Śaṅkara specifies it as the impurity/turbidity of non-discrimination that defiles self/not-self discernment.
One might take śrotavyasya śrutasya ca as merely ‘scriptures heard and to be heard’; Śaṅkara’s paraphrase emphasizes their appearing niṣphala, fruitless, to the seeker at that stage.
analyzer_disagreements: te: ByT5 only marked tvad_SG; Śaṅkara’s te tava fixes the case as genitive singular. The form is not gender-distinct; Pum is supplied contextually for Arjuna.
vyatitariṣyati: ByT5 gives the prefixed lemma vyatitṛ; per the requested format this is analyzed as bare root tṝ with prefixes vi + ati.
gantāsi: ByT5 marks it as simple future, but the form is the periphrastic future (Luṭ) of √gam; the simple future would be gamiṣyasi.
śrotavyasya: ByT5 gives root śru with gerundive information; for the required subanta analysis the inflected nominal stem is śrotavya, neuter genitive singular.
śrutasya: ByT5 gives root śru with participial information; for the required subanta analysis the inflected nominal stem is śruta, neuter genitive singular.
mula: yadā te moha-kalilaṃ buddhir vyatitariṣyati | tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
commentary_lines: yadā yasmin kāle te tava moha-kalilaṃ mohātmakam aviveka-rūpaṃ kāluṣyaṃ yena ātmānātma-viveka-bodhaṃ kaluṣīkṛtya viṣayaṃ pratyantaḥ-karaṇaṃ pravartate, tat tava buddhiḥ vyatitariṣyati vyatikramiṣyati, atiśuddha-bhāvam āpātryate ity arthaḥ |
tadā tasmin kāle gantāsi prāpsyasi nirvedaṃ vairāgyaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca, tadā śrotavyaṃ śrutaṃ ca te niṣphalaṃ pratibhātīty abhiprāyaḥ ||bhgs_2.52||
